Title:
Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
16 pages, 8 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers several times per token and, under fixed-depth inference, run the same number of loops when they prefill the prompt and when they decode each answer token. We untie the two. A small loop adapter trained on a frozen looped model lets it prefill with m loops and decode with n: one set of parameters serves all 16 pairs up to four loops, and one stored prompt KV cache serves every decode loop. On the checkpoints and benchmarks we test, the two counts buy different things: prefill loops mainly raise knowledge and long-context benchmarks (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, RULER, HELMET), decode loops mainly raise multi-step math (GSM8K, MATH-500), with exceptions that depend on the task and its prompt. On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, prefill 4 / decode 2 scores at least as high as the native two-loop model on all eight standard benchmarks we test (significantly higher on five), at the same decode cost, and within two points of the native four-loop model on six; on GSM8K it is 1.0 point below the four-loop model on the full test set and, on 64 timed problems, answers in 0.55x its time. Untying the loops also makes looped decision models more accurate when they decide with one loop, against a control continued with the same data and updates. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow
